pages.text: "I will move it by myself!" Nils the little bear tapped a log lying on the leaves. It was much longer than he was. "Grandpa, you just watch!"
Nils hugged the end of the log and pulled. Strain, strain! It would not budge. His booted feet slid over the wet leaves.
This time he pushed with his shoulder. Heave-ho! Heave-ho! The log rolled a handspan, then caught on a tree root. Even after three more tries, it would not move from there.
Nils plopped down on the leaves. He was panting, and his paws trembled. "The shed is still so far away..."
Grandpa Bruno came over and sat at the opposite end. "Nils, you hold this end, and I will hold the other." Nils tilted his head. "Will that make it lighter?"
They each lifted an end. Up came the log! "Oh, it is light!" Nils opened his eyes wide. "Together, heave-ho!" Grandpa called in time with him.
"Together, heave-ho! Together, heave-ho!" Their steps matched the rhythm too. The log traveled along the forest path all the way to the shed.
Thump! They put the log down in front of the shed. Nils sat on it, swinging his legs. "Alone, I could not even move it a handspan. Together, we came all the way!"
In the evening, they moved a sack of potatoes. It was too full for Nils to lift alone. "One, ask when it is hard! Two, hold one end each! Three, call together!" Nils gripped one end first.
Grandpa lifted Nils onto his shoulders. Together, they could do things Nils could not do alone. Nils raised both paws high above his head. "Together, heave-ho! Let us work together tomorrow too!"
